stem: A client with small-cell lung cancer develops new euvolemic hyponatremia. Which paraneoplastic complication should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH)

rationale: SIADH causes inappropriate vasopressin/antidiuretic hormone activity that impairs renal free-water excretion, producing hyponatremia; affected clients are commonly euvolemic. Ectopic vasopressin production is particularly associated with small-cell lung carcinoma. Diabetes insipidus causes excessive free-water loss rather than SIADH-type hyponatremia, primary hyperparathyroidism is a calcium disorder, and tumor lysis syndrome has a different metabolic pattern. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Recognize euvolemic hyponatremia in a client with small-cell lung cancer as a possible manifestation of SIADH from ectopic vasopressin production.
